correctness.rationale: The prefix property is factorial for richness and additive-cube-freeness. On extension by a symbol, all new cubes end at the last position and are exactly those equal integer-sum triples checked with prefix sums; preservation of richness is equivalent to introduction of one previously unseen palindrome as longest palindromic suffix. To avoid dependence on packaged palindromic-tree implementation, wrote and compiled an independent C++ DFS with explicit suffix-palindrome string matching and a set of all previously occurring palindromes. It explored all 404535 admissible prefixes, independently recovering N(100..105)=(90,80,36,12,8,0) and the eight explicit length-104 words. An independent Python orbit check verifies reversal and a→2−a preserve those words and form exactly two four-word orbits. Any longer word would have an admissible 105-prefix, which the exhaustive search rules out; not an extrapolation from finite prefix samples.

originality.rationale: Andrade–Mol, arXiv:2408.15390v2 (full relevant sections read), treats rich ternary words avoiding abelian cubes; the published longest such word has length 180. Weighted additive-cube-freeness is strictly stronger than abelian-cube-freeness: equality of Parikh vectors implies equal sums but not conversely. Theorem 1.2 in Andrade–Mol on infinite additive-fourth-power-free rich words does not bar additive cubes. Thus neither published 180 nor fourth-power avoidance implies 104, eight words or two orbits. Resultary rich-word retrievals and exact 104/8 web searches returned different word properties, not this census. Priority is best-of-knowledge, not proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact enumeration of the same weighted additive-cube-free rich words might predate this census.
The exhaustive computation is a finite machine-assisted proof; replay relies on deterministic integer operations but does not establish an infinite-word theorem.

value.rationale: An exact extremal threshold for naturally defined palindromically rich ternary words under additive cube avoidance settles a mathematically motivated finite endpoint absent from the nearby abelian-cube classification. The eight explicit equality words and reversal/complement orbits are usable as tests of structural hypotheses about rich avoiders. It is neither arbitrary alphabet reweighting nor recomputation of the different 180 bound.

limitations: Only ordinary integer alphabet {0,1,2} and additive cubes, not arbitrary symbol relabelings.
